summary: Geoff Childs is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Indiana University, studying under Tsetan Chonjore, and held posts at the Australian National University and Washington University in St. Louis.

Geoffrey Barstow is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held a post at the University of Virginia around 2006 to 2013 and became assistant professor of religious studies at Oregon State University around 2014.

Geoffrey Goble works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned an MA from the University of Virginia and a PhD from Indiana University, and was appointed Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Oklahoma (attested 2019).

Geoffrey Samuel is a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Cambridge under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, Peter J. Wilson, and Edmund Leach, later holding professorships at Newcastle, Lancaster, and Cardiff University.

Georg Buddruss (1929–2021) was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt and the University of Tübingen, serving as professor at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz from around 1963 to 1997.

Georg Bühler (1837–1898) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and Hermann Sauppe. He held chairs at Elphinstone College, Deccan College, the University of Mumbai, and the University of Vienna.

Georg Curtius (1820–1885) was a linguist who studied at Bonn under Ritschl and Lassen and at Berlin under Bopp. He held academic posts at Charles University and the University of Kiel before serving as professor at Leipzig University (~1862–1885).

Georg Morgenstierne (1892–1978) was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Oslo and under Sten Konow, later holding a post at the University of Gothenburg (~1930–1937).

Georg Wilhelm Freytag (1788–1861) was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at the University of Göttingen and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, holding posts at the University of Göttingen (~1811–1815) and the University of Bonn (~1819–1861).

Georg von Simson (1933–) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He was an editor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1968 and served as professor at the University of Oslo from around 1977 to 2003.

Georg von der Gabelentz (1840–1893) was a scholar in sinology and linguistics. He studied at the universities of Jena and Leipzig, later serving as professor of East Asian languages at Leipzig University and at Humboldt University of Berlin.

George A. Keyworth (1970–) specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He studied at UCSB and UCLA (PhD under Robert E. Buswell Jr.) and held posts at the University of Colorado Boulder and the University of Saskatchewan.
George Abraham Grierson (1851–1941) was a linguist and Indologist. He was educated at St. Bees School and Trinity College Dublin, and served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1873 to 1902.

George Baumann (1936–) is an Indologist who earned his PhD from Heidelberg University (~1968–1973). He served as Head of the Oriental Department at Tübingen University Library from 1976 to 2001 and at the University of Tübingen.

George Cardona (1936–2024) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at New York University and Yale University. He was a fellow at CASBS (1971–1972) and spent his career as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania.

George Chemparathy (1928–2011) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Erich Frauwallner and Paul Hacker. He held posts at Loyola College, Chennai, and served as professor at Utrecht University from around 1974 to 1993.

George Cœdès (1886–1969) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1903–1906) and served as president of the Société des Amis du Vieux Hanoi (attested 1934).

George D. Bond (1942–) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the University of Sri Lanka and Northwestern University, where he completed his PhD and served as Professor of Religion from around 1974 to 2011.

George Foot Moore (1851–1931) was a scholar of religious studies who studied at Yale University (~1868–1872). He served as professor at Andover Theological Seminary (~1883–1901) and at Harvard University (~1902–1928).

George L. Hart (1942–) is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harvard University (~1963–1969). He held an academic post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1969–1975) before serving as professor at UC Berkeley (~1975–2013).
